codes.watering: The rooms that the batch held get water again when its hardware reads off.
causes: The mix pump did not start, or its power plug did not switch.
The power sensor is offline, or it reports slowly.
The minimum power is set above the power of the pump.
fixes: WARNING: Isolate the electrical power before you touch a pump, a valve or its wiring. Water near mains power can cause an electric shock.
Check the mix pump and its power plug.
Read the power sensor while the pump runs.
Set the minimum power below the power of the pump.
To skip the power check, set the minimum power to 0.

codes.title: Stopped batch or dose
codes.meaning: A batch stopped before its end, or a dose needs a check. The cause can be a person, a failed step, a device that did not read off, or the batch watchdog. The alert names the step, the reason and what the controller dosed.
codes.watering: The controller sets all the dosing pumps, the fill valve, the mix pump and the mix valves to off. The rooms that the batch held get water again when its hardware and its hold read off. The alert comes again each 30 min until then.
causes: A person stopped the batch.
A fill, a mix or a dose failed.
A switch of the batch, or of a room that the batch holds, did not read off.
The volume number of a pump did not go back to its earlier value.
The filled-at entity or the hold entity did not accept its command.
The controller has an error. Its log names the error.
fixes: WARNING: Wear gloves and eye protection when you touch the batch tank or the stock tanks. Concentrated nutrients and pH adjusters can injure the skin and the eyes.
CAUTION: Do not make a full new batch before you examine the tank. The tank can already contain part of the dose.
Examine the batch tank before you make a new batch.
Read what the controller dosed before the stop.
Correct the cause that the alert names.
Make the batch again.
If the alert says that a volume number was not restored, set it by hand before the next batch.
If the alert names a controller error, read the controller log.

codes.title: Stock draw not recorded
codes.meaning: A dose took nutrient from a stock tank, but Home Assistant did not record the draw. The tank is not linked to the room, Home Assistant refused the draw, or 24 h passed. The dosing history of the room keeps the draw.
codes.watering: Water continues as usual. The level of the stock tank shows more than the tank contains.
causes: A person removed the stock tank after the pump was linked to it.
The stock service of Crop Steering refused the call, or it was not available at that time (an old integration, or a reload).
The controller could not connect to Home Assistant for 24 h.
fixes: In Stock tanks, use Set level to enter the real level of the tank.
Check the stock tank of the pump in the dosing setup.

codes.title: Batch mix outside band
codes.meaning: After the mix of a batch stopped, the controller waited 5 min and read the tank with the feed EC and feed pH probes. A reading was outside the EC or pH band of the room, or a probe gave no usable reading. The controller does not mark the batch good.
codes.watering: The mix check never holds the water. The source-water gate holds the water by itself when the feed probe reads outside its band. The controller refuses an automatic batch until a batch made by hand passes the check.
causes: A recipe quantity, a stock tank or a dosing pump is incorrect.
A fill gave too much or too little water.
The feed EC or feed pH band is for a different growth stage.
A feed probe is offline, needs calibration, or reports in ppm.
fixes: WARNING: Wear gloves and eye protection when you touch the batch tank or the stock tanks. Concentrated nutrients and pH adjusters can injure the skin and the eyes.
CAUTION: Correct the batch before you water from it. A wrong feed EC or feed pH can damage the roots.
Measure the tank with a hand-held meter.
Correct the tank with single doses or fresh water.
Check the recipe, the stock tanks and the EC and pH bands.
Calibrate the feed probe, or connect it again.
Set the probe to report mS/cm or µS/cm, not ppm.
Make the next batch by hand.

codes.title: Tank pH not corrected
codes.meaning: pH auto-correct is on, and the batch tank read outside the feed pH band of the room. A correction did not bring the tank into the band: a dose did not move the pH, the pH went past the other side of the band, the probe could not be read after the mix, the doses were not enough, or the correction stopped. Or the controller could not start a correction (for example no pump has the pH role, there is no mixing pump, or the doses of the day are used).
codes.watering: The source-water gate holds the shots while the feed pH is outside its band. After a failed correction, pH auto-correct is locked for this tank: it doses no more until a person switches it off and on again, or the tank is filled again.
causes: The pH probe needs calibration, or it is dirty or offline.
The pH pump is empty, blocked, or not calibrated.
The pH adjuster is too weak or too strong for the dose size.
No dosing pump has the pH up or pH down role, or the tank has no mixing pump.
fixes: WARNING: Wear gloves and eye protection when you touch the batch tank or a pH adjuster. pH adjusters can injure the skin and the eyes.
Measure the tank with a hand-held meter, and correct it by hand.
Calibrate or clean the pH probe.
Check the pH pump, its stock and its calibration.
Change the dose length or the number of doses in the pH auto-correct settings of the room.
Switch pH auto-correct off and on again to unlock it.

codes.title: Lights dimmed on dry substrate
codes.meaning: Dimming on dry substrate is on. A zone read under the dry floor with the lights on, and the controller dimmed the light of the room. Or the controller set the light back, or another controller changed the light while it was dimmed, so the controller no longer dims or restores it.
codes.watering: The alert does not change the water. A dimmed light slows the drying of the substrate. The controller never switches a light off or on, and never dims below 30%.
causes: A hold stops the shots of a zone, the tank is empty, or a dripper is blocked.
The dry floor is too high for the substrate.
Another automation or a person changed the light while it was dimmed.
fixes: Find out why the zone is dry, and water it.
Check the brightness of the light.
Change the dry floor, the dim level or the delay in the settings of the room, or switch dimming off.

codes.title: Light dimmed too long
codes.meaning: The light of the room stayed dimmed for the longest time that you set (4 h by default), and the controller set it back. Or the light did not come back to its brightness when the controller asked.
codes.watering: The alert does not change the water. The zone that was dry is probably still dry.
causes: A hold stops the shots of a zone for a long time.
The light is offline, or does not accept a brightness.
fixes: CAUTION: Do not ignore this alert. The substrate of the zone is dry.
Find out why the zone is dry, and water it by hand if needed.
Check the light, and set its brightness by hand.

codes.title: Tank at minimum level
codes.meaning: The tank level of this room is 8% or less, or its low float switch reads low. This check works only when a tank level entity is mapped in Rooms and setup.
codes.watering: The controller holds each zone of the room, so the pump does not run dry. Water starts again when the tank is at 12% or more and the float switch does not read low.
causes: The tank became empty, because nobody refilled it in time. CS-903 tells you before the refill is necessary.
A fill did not occur, or it stopped early.
The full and empty distances of the tank are incorrect, so the level reads lower than the real level.
fixes: CAUTION: Do not start the pump by hand while the tank is at its minimum. The pump can run dry and break.
Refill the tank.
Check the full and empty distances of the tank in Crop Steering → Rooms and setup.
Check the low state of the float switch.

codes.title: Tank level not readable
codes.meaning: The tank level of this room gives no usable reading, or the distance sensor seems stuck. The shots took enough water to decrease the level, but the reading did not change. The controller cannot know how much water remains.
codes.watering: The controller holds each zone of the room until the level reads again, or until a stuck sensor moves. This hold prevents a pump that runs dry.
causes: The sensor has no power, or it lost its connection to Home Assistant.
The distance sensor is stuck: an object is in its beam, it has condensation, or its reading stays high.
fixes: CAUTION: Do not remove the tank level only to start the water again. Without a level, the pump can run dry.
Check the sensor, its power and its position.
Make sure that Home Assistant shows a reading.
Remove condensation or objects from the sensor beam.
If the room must water without a tank level, remove the level entity in Crop Steering → Rooms and setup.

codes.title: Refill needed before next shots
codes.meaning: One more set of shots, the last shot of each zone, takes the tank to its 8% minimum or below. The controller calculates this from the litres for each 1% that the tank showed, and needs a distance sensor for it.
codes.watering: Water continues. A shot that takes the tank to its minimum waits until you refill the tank. The card clears when the tank has enough water for a full set of shots.
causes: The tank level decreases, as it does between refills.
fixes: Refill the tank, or start a batch.

codes.title: Tank above full mark
codes.meaning: The tank level reads 102% or more of its full distance.
codes.watering: Water continues. The controller closes the fill valve of a batch, and does not open it until the level reads 98% or less.
causes: The fill valve did not close, or it leaks.
The full distance of the tank is set too far down, so a full tank reads more than 100%.
fixes: CAUTION: Examine the tank and the fill valve now. A fill valve that leaks can overflow the tank.
Make sure that the fill valve closes fully.
Check the full distance of the tank in Crop Steering → Rooms and setup.

codes.title: Estimated tank level low
codes.meaning: The room has no tank level sensor, and a Tank size (estimate) above 0. From the litres that the shots used since the tank was last filled, the tank is at or below the room setting Estimated tank low alert (20% by default). The litres come from the dripper flow settings, not from a measurement.
codes.watering: The alert does not change the water. The estimate never holds a shot.
causes: The tank level decreases, as it does between refills.
The tank was filled and Tank filled was not pressed.
The dripper flow settings are higher than the real flow.
fixes: Refill the tank, then press Tank filled.
If the estimate is often wrong, check the dripper flow settings, or map a tank level sensor in Rooms and setup.

codes.title: Batch tank low
codes.meaning: The batch tank of the room read at or below its refill reminder level (remind_pct) 3 times, 1 min apart. Nothing refills the tank automatically.
codes.watering: Water continues as usual. The reminder clears when the level is 5 points above the reminder level. It comes again each day while the level stays low.
causes: The shots of the room took water from the batch tank since the last fill.
fixes: Refill the tank by hand, or make a batch.
To stop the reminders, set the refill reminder to 0% in the dosing setup.

codes.title: EC flushing off, feed EC unknown
codes.meaning: The room has no feed EC probe, and the feed recipe in use declares no feed EC. The controller does not know the EC of the feed water.
codes.watering: The zones get water on their VWC only. The controller does not flush high pore EC and does not hold a zone for high EC, because it cannot tell if the feed can decrease the pore EC. The alert comes once and goes when the room gets a feed EC.
causes: No feed EC probe is set for the room in the controller app options (feed_ec_sensor).
The feed recipe in use has no EC, or the room has no dosing setup.
fixes: CAUTION: Do not ignore this alert for many days. Salt can build up in the substrate when the controller cannot flush.
Set the feed EC on the feed recipe in use (Crop Steering → Dosing), or set a feed EC probe in the controller app options.
